5954.t: Traditionally derived from πλατύς (plătŭ́s, “broad; flat”), or taken to be inherited directly from Proto-Indo-European *pl̥th₂enós (“wide; broad”), under the assumption that the tree was named after its broad leaves or flat patches of bark.

5924.t: From περί (perí). Compare περικαλλής (perikallḗs, “very beautiful”), Latin permagnus (“very great”) etc.

5958.t: No clear etymology. Earlier attempts to analyze the formation as a conflation of several different verbs are unconvincing.

5949.t: The etymological base of the word is not clear. Formally, there is no reason to disconnect the word from πλάσσω (plássō, “to knead, mold”), but this linkage is not evident on the semantic side.

5920.t: Derived from πέλεκυς (pélekus, “axe”), because of the functional and/or formal similarity with an axe.

5952.t: Verbal adjective, from πλώω (plṓō, “to sail, float”) + -τός (-tós).

5976.t: From the root of ποιμήν (poimḗn, “shepherd”) + -η (-ē), from Proto-Indo-European *peh₂- (“to protect, shepherd”).
